chronoseries.note: Singleton extant node. The comparison that changes at this slot is the detail-scale wavelength versus the 10 µm tier center, not a fossil chronospecies.

pde: du/dt = D_u laplacian(u) + a - u + u^2 v
dv/dt = D_v laplacian(v) + b - u^2 v
equations.delta: D_u D_v k^4 - (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) k^2 + (f_u g_v - f_v g_u)
equations.k_star: argmax_k sigma_plus(k), calibrated to 2 pi / 16 um

parameters.boundary_condition: periodic square for the bulk PDE; circular front mask for the ocellus reconstruction

reported_in_source: Turing 1952: a reaction-diffusion system selects a finite critical wavenumber.
Kawasaki et al. 1997 and Golding et al. 1998: Bacillus subtilis colony outlines are reproducible with reaction-diffusion models at colony scale.
Ben-Jacob, Cohen and Levine 2000: branching bacterial colonies are a cooperative pattern-forming system.
Kondo and Miura 2010: biological periodic patterns are usefully read as RD wavelength selection.
Sharpe et al. 1998 and Dion et al. 2019: B. subtilis has a characteristic cell length and diameter, so 16 µm spans a few rods.
does_not_claim: That any cited paper measured a 16 µm pigment or ocellus wavelength in B. subtilis.
That the Korinna 2019 micrograph contains a scale bar from which R = 183 µm was read.
That the kinematic front reconstruction is a pixel-level solution of the bulk PDE.
